name: Wendy Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I play cello for a busy wedding quartet, record slow practice lines and teach three adults. I have a music degree and twenty-nine years of paid playing. The best moment is when a nervous couple hears their chosen tune start exactly as the doors open.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does that work fit at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 58, my partner has regular shifts at a bus depot and our children are grown. We own our flat and have eleven months of expenses saved. My fees are high for a working musician, and there are plenty of other groups nearby, though their chairs are not promised. I use AI occasionally for date drafts after others have checked a tool, then verify them against signed contracts.

say: I'd accept **faster dates** with rehearsal and travel fees on the contract.
I'd say the **wedding tune** still needs a player watching the entrance.
think: Our **eleven-month reserve** and partner wage cover one moved wedding.
The **quartet and lessons** should keep paying in mild AI.
do: Confirm **six paid ceremonies** and three lessons; retain written cancellation terms.
Check **AI date drafts** against signed bookings and save a quarter of extra cleared fees after essentials.
feel: I feel **calm** while paid ceremonies and household wages hold.
S0.quote: A wedding tune still needs someone to watch the couple enter.
fieldNote: Her **higher musician pay** and eleven-month reserve buffer a moved ceremony without threatening regular household bills.
Occasional **AI date drafts** are checked against contracts without guest lists.

steps.text: Confirm six paid ceremonies and three lessons; retain written cancellation terms
Check AI dates against contracts; save quarter of extra cleared ceremony after flat charges/food/bow repairs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the quartet faster dates are helpful if the paid rehearsal and travel fee stay on the contract. A wedding tune still needs someone to watch the couple enter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Eleven months saved and my partner's regular wage make one moved wedding manageable. In this mild picture I expect the quartet and lessons to keep paying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll confirm the next six paid ceremonies and three adult lessons, and ask the booker to keep cancellation pay in each contract. In the first year of this small change I'll check occasional AI date drafts against the signed bookings and save a quarter of each extra cleared ceremony fee after flat charges, food and bow repairs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the work we have. A shifted wedding would be troublesome, but the bills would still be paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when a ceremony moved?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One couple moved a ceremony by two weeks last spring. The written term paid half the playing fee and the travel already spent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What data goes into a date draft?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A date draft does not need a guest list. I check the time, hall and paid fee against the signed paper.

say: I'd ask whether **generated practice lines** replace paid recordings.
I'd request **separate written fees** for playing and preparation.
think: Practice tracks provide **one fifth** of my own pay.
Our **eleven-month reserve** buys search time, not permanent replacement income.
do: Compare **twelve invoices** with new orders and request signed paid ceremonies.
Seek **extra written-rate calls** only if tracks fall and venues actually book them; keep current pupils.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a realistic cut to recording fees.
S1.quote: A spare hour in my diary is no use until somebody books it for pay.
fieldNote: Her **replacement plan** counts only signed paid quartet calls, never a free hour.
She **waits for proven AI** and would require paid demonstration, owned nameless music, permitted use and manual checks.

steps.text: Compare twelve track invoices and request three months of signed paid ceremonies
Offer freed hours for extra written-rate quartet calls only after track cuts and real bookings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the quartet booker whether generated practice lines will replace my paid recordings. I would want the playing and preparation fees written separately before signing a new season.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Practice recordings bring about a fifth of my pay. If orders fall, eleven months saved and many local groups give me time to ask for more paid playing, but the missing fifth would still matter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll compare twelve practice-track invoices with new orders and ask for three months of signed paid ceremonies. In the first year, if tracks decline, I'll offer those freed hours for extra quartet calls only at a written rate and keep my existing pupils; I will not buy an AI trial before a paid trusted-player demonstration on safe music.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a real cut to recording fees. A spare hour in my diary is no use until somebody books it for pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a safe tool demonstration require?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A trusted player would need to show a tool on music they own without names, under a paid-use licence and approved storage. I would play its edits before trusting any note.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Are extra quartet calls booked?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the extra calls have not been booked yet. I'll count only a signed paid ceremony in our budget.

say: I'd distinguish **2028 thinking AGI** from 2031 cello-playing robots.
I'd put **live wedding fees** in writing while ceremonies remain booked.
think: I expect **one-fifth pay** from practice tracks to end in 2028.
Further **live wedding cuts** remain possible, not expected.
do: Total **track fees**, request signed wedding dates and actual pension statements before stopping work.
Seek **posted tutor work** after 2028 live cuts only if degree/teaching qualify, written net after travel replaces losses and buses fit.
Keep **quartet and pupils** until a suitable signed offer arrives.
feel: I feel **anxious** about expected track loss with time to search.
S2.quote: Eleven months saved do not tell me what pension income would reach the bank each month.
fieldNote: Expected **2028 track loss** precedes 2031 playing robots; live cuts remain conditional.
A tutor role needs **posted eligibility**, written replacement net after travel, bus access and signed offer.

steps.text: Total track fees; request signed paid wedding dates and actual pension statements
Seek posted tutor job after live cuts if music degree/teaching qualify and buses fit
Require written net after travel replacing losses; keep quartet/pupils until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the quartet that thinking AGI by 2028 could make practice lines before a robot can bow a cello. Cello-playing robots follow around 2031, so I would put the live wedding fees in writing now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the practice-track orders to stop in 2028 and remove a fifth of my pay. Live weddings might fall as well, but the signed ceremonies we have are real today.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll total track fees, ask for signed paid wedding dates and request actual pension statements before discussing any stop at 60. In the first year after 2028, if live calls also fall, I'll seek a posted paid music-centre tutor role only if my degree and teaching experience qualify, written net pay after travel replaces lost fees and buses fit the hours; I'll keep quartet and pupils until a suitable offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the expected fifth of my pay disappearing, with savings and nearby employers allowing a search. I would be alarmed if signed live bookings also collapsed, but that is not my forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is a music-centre tutor role open now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No centre has offered me a tutor post. I would read current paid hours and qualification rules before applying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you know your pension income?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have not seen our pension statements. Eleven months saved do not tell me what pension income would reach the bank each month.

say: I'd seek **paid cello maintenance learning** during the warning years.
I'd place **playing robots** around 2034 after track changes.
think: Ordinary software could cheapen **practice tracks before 2031**, ahead of playing robots.
I need **recognized supervised training** before bridge or solvent work.
do: Confirm **shop recognition** before enrolling; take actual paid funded place only with protected quartet/pupil wages, safety gear and qualified supervision.
Seek **posted repair work** after both 2031 track/wedding cuts if certificate qualifies; written replacement net after travel, buses fit.
Keep **quartet and pupils** until signed offer; handle bridges/solvents under repairer until signed safety approval.
feel: I feel **anxious** until training and paid work are real.
S3.quote: A cello-repair certificate that no local shop accepts would not replace a wedding fee.
fieldNote: The **repair course** needs prior local shop recognition, actual paid funded place and no lost quartet or pupil wages.
The **new work** requires qualified supervision, signed safety checks, posted paid role and written replacement net after travel.

steps.text: Confirm local shops accept cello-repair certificate before enrolling in paid funded place with protected quartet/pupil wages
Work under qualified repairer with safety gear until bridge/solvent checks receive signed approval
Seek posted repair-assistant after both track/wedding cuts if certificate qualifies and buses fit
Require written net after travel replacing losses; keep quartet/pupils until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the quartet that five years to AGI by 2031 gives me time to learn paid cello maintenance from a repairer. Cello-playing robots follow around 2034, after software has altered the practice tracks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ordinary software could cheapen tracks before 2031. I know how to change a string, but I would not set a bridge, the wooden support under the strings, or use varnish solvents without a trained repairer beside me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I'll check whether local instrument shops accept a six-month cello-repair certificate before enrolling. I'll take an actual paid workshop place only if the shop funds tuition and safety gear, wages match any quartet dates or pupil hours displaced, and a qualified repairer supervises bridge and solvent work. In the first year after 2031, if tracks end and paid weddings also fall, I'll seek a posted paid repair-assistant role only if the certificate qualifies, written net pay after travel replaces lost fees and buses run after shifts; I'll keep quartet and pupils until a suitable signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious until the paid place and a real repair job exist. A cello-repair certificate that no local shop accepts would not replace a wedding fee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you repair a cello alone afterward?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would not set someone else's cello bridge alone after the course. The repairer must inspect my first work and sign the safety checklist before I take responsibility.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if tuition is free but wages fall?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the workshop is free but wages fall below displaced wedding and pupil fees, I'll wait for another intake. Eleven months saved are for household shocks, not unpaid tuition time.

Our **eleven-month reserve** does not prove retirement income covers bills.

Seek **degree/teaching-qualified cello-tutor job** after 2036 live cuts and pension gap; posted pay, written replacement net after travel, buses fit.

S4.quote: I will decide how much to slow only after reading my pension statement alongside signed wedding bookings.
fieldNote: Her **fifteen-month target** uses genuine extra cleared wedding fees after essentials.
A **tutor move** needs real paid posting, degree/teaching fit, written replacement net after travel, buses and signed offer.

steps.text: Request actual pension statements and written two-year paid wedding-call plan
Save 25% of extra cleared ceremony fees after flat-charges/food/cello repairs toward fifteen months
Keep paid weddings/pupils after 2036 until suitable signed offer
Seek degree/teaching-qualified posted tutor after live cuts and pension gap; written replacement net after travel, buses

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my grown children ten years to AGI by 2036 is time to see real pension figures and written wedding bookings. Cello-playing robots follow around 2039, but a birthday cannot sign a cheque.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I might still want quartet and pupil work. Eleven months saved and our flat give comfort now, yet I do not know whether an actual pension covers our regular bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll request actual pension statements and a written two-year paid-call plan, then save a quarter of each extra cleared ceremony fee after flat charges, food and cello repairs toward fifteen months of expenses. In the first year after 2036 I'll keep paid weddings and pupils while booked; if live pay falls and pension figures leave a gap, I'll seek a posted paid cello-tutor job only if my degree and teaching qualify, written net pay after travel replaces lost fees and buses fit, keeping current work until a suitable signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant pay mix while current bookings and savings are strong. I will decide how much to slow only after reading my pension statement alongside signed wedding bookings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no extra ceremony pays?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If no extra ceremony pays, nothing from that source goes into savings. I will not move food money just to meet fifteen months.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Have you seen the pension amount?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I have not received the pension amount. I will read the statement with my partner before giving up paid calls.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because practice tracks could end before another paid role opens. Signed wedding dates, actual pension figures and a posted qualifying teaching role with written net pay after travel would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who signs off the first repaired bridge after a course. The wooden bridge holding up cello strings can fall even when a repairer's certificate looks fine.

headlineQuote: The wooden bridge holding up cello strings can fall even when a repairer's certificate looks fine.
portrait: Wendy is a **58-year-old experienced cellist** with a music degree, partner and grown children.
Her **higher pay**, eleven-month reserve and many nearby groups provide time to replace recording losses.
She uses **AI occasionally** for dates and learns cello repair only after local recognition and paid supervised instruction.
She checks **actual pension figures** before reducing paid wedding or pupil work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase one fifth of Wendy's pay from practice tracks.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed weddings**, actual pension figures and posted qualifying teaching with written after-travel replacement pay would help.
